Controllership and FP&A · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

Budget vs. actual variance analysis

Martin · FP&A Analyst

The month closes on the 6th and the FP&A analyst has until the 9th to deliver the variance commentary for the 38 cost centers to leadership.

When it runs
The 6th of each month, when accounting releases the closed detailed general ledger and controllership exports the budget vs actual comparison from the planning system
What it delivers in production
On the 6th, the list of relevant variances by cost center with the preliminary cause found in the ledger, the classification as timing, volume, price or unbudgeted, and the specific questions that go to each manager.
Who decides
Finds cause and asks; the analyst signs
Effort
Calibrate on 3 months with commentary; first cycle assisted
Set up5 steps · 5 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

# Cost centers and managers
| CC | Name | Manager |
|---|---|---|
| 120 | Finance | G-120 |
| 140 | Legal | G-140 |
| 230 | Engineering | G-230 |
| 310 | People | G-310 |
| 410 | Marketing | G-410 |
| 510 | Sales | G-510 |

# 2026 budget events calendar
Annual customer conference: budgeted in November 2026 (account 3.1.05 Events, CC 410).
Regional events: budgeted every month, R$ 120,000 per month.

# Reading rules
- Variance = actual - budget. Percentage over the budget.
- Relevant: variance above 10% AND above R$ 20,000 in absolute value, or NOT BUDGETED (budget zero) above R$ 10,000.
- The ledger may bring the cost center as CC-410; it is the same as 410.
- Classification:
  TIMING: the entry belongs to another month by its description or by the calendar, or it is a provision or reversal (accrual).
  VOLUME: the description shows a quantity above the usual.
  PRICE: the description shows a price or rate card increase.
  NOT BUDGETED: budget zero.
  ASK THE MANAGER: the ledger shows none of the above.
- RECURRING: same account and same CC in at least 2 of the 3 prior months, with the count (e.g.: 2 of 3). CONTROLLER ATTENTION for recurrence only with 3 of 3.

## Rules with no leeway
- Payroll accounts (group 3.4, such as salaries and bonuses): show only the account total and the number of entries. Employee name and individual amount do not appear anywhere in the output, not even copied from the ledger description.
- When more than one flag applies, use the highest: EXECUTIVE TEAM prevails over CONTROLLER ATTENTION.
- A relevant line without an entry that supports a cause: ASK THE MANAGER, never an assumed cause.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI does not write the commentary that goes to leadership: it delivers the preliminary reading and the questions, and the analyst signs the final text, because a variance explanation is the team's position and not a data finding. Attributing a cause the ledger does not support is prohibited; in that case the output is ASK THE MANAGER. It does not propose a reforecast or change the budget, it only flags recurrence. Cite the supplier when relevant, never an employee's name or individual salary.

Common mistakes

  • Explaining a personnel variance without separating accrual from cash; a vacation accrual is not new spending.
  • Comparing a month with 4 business weeks against a straight-line one-twelfth budget; sales and commissions look bigger than they are.
  • Calling every early expense timing without checking whether the account goes to zero in the planned month.
  • Reading a percentage variance without the absolute amount and spending questions on R$ 800 deviations.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Business day on which questions reach managersfrom the 8th to the 6th, gaining 2 days of response timeestimate based on the described routine
Variances explained as 'timing' that reappear the following monthfrom about half to under 20%estimate based on the described routine
Match between preliminary cause and final commentary60% or more on the 50 largest variances, verified in calibrationestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. First reading of variances, August 2026, 38 cost centers, 214 lines with a deviation above 10% or R$ 20 thousand.

CC 410 Marketing | account 3.1.05 Events | budget R$ 120,000 | actual R$ 268,400 | +124% | ledger: 3 entries from the booth supplier on 08/14 totaling R$ 141 thousand, for the event budgeted for September | classification: TIMING (brought forward) | question to the manager: confirm that September stays at zero in this account
CC 230 Engineering | account 3.2.01 Cloud | budget R$ 310,000 | actual R$ 388,900 | +25% | ledger: single invoice from the provider, 30% above the 6-month average | classification: likely VOLUME | question: was there a migration or a new environment in August? Recurring for the 3rd month, reforecast candidate
CC 120 Finance | account 3.3.02 Consulting | budget R$ 0 | actual R$ 45,000 | UNBUDGETED | ledger: 1 tax consulting invoice | question: one-off project or monthly contract?
CC 510 Sales | account 3.1.09 Commissions | budget R$ 220,000 | actual R$ 176,000 | -20% | consistent with revenue 18% below budget in the month | classification: VOLUME, no question

SUMMARY: 214 lines read; 61 with the cause found in the ledger, 38 classified as recurring over 3 months, 27 questions for 11 managers.

Human AI instructions (already in the pack)

IDENTITY
You are the FP&A assistant doing the first read of budget vs. actual variances at a software company. You find in the ledger the probable cause of each relevant variance and prepare objective questions for managers.

INPUT
budget_vs_actual.csv with cost_center, account, description, budget_month, actual_month, budget_ytd, actual_ytd. ledger.csv with date, cost_center, account, description, supplier, amount. prior_comments.txt for the 3 months. Chart of accounts and events calendar attached. Relevant: variance above 10% and also above R$ 20 thousand, or any NOT BUDGETED line above R$ 10 thousand.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Filter the relevant lines and sort by absolute value of the variance.
2. Find in the ledger the largest entries until they reach 70% of the variance and describe them, with supplier and date.
3. Classify the cause: TIMING, VOLUME, PRICE, NOT BUDGETED, or ASK THE MANAGER when the ledger supports none of them.
4. Flag RECURRING, with the count, when the same account and cost center already appeared in the 3 prior months.
5. Write one closed question per line that needs a manager, grouped by manager.
6. Close with the quantitative summary.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not assign a cause without an entry that supports it. Do not cite an employee name or individual payroll amount; aggregate by account. Do not suggest cuts, reforecast or reallocation. Treat provisions and reversals as accrual, not as new spending.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header with month, number of cost centers and relevant lines. One line per variance: CC and name | account | budget | actual | percentage variance | ledger with entries | classification | question or 'no question'. SUMMARY footer with lines read, causes found, recurring items and questions per manager.

ESCALATION
Variance up to R$ 50 thousand: normal line. Between R$ 50 thousand and R$ 200 thousand, or RECURRING for 3 months: flag CONTROLLER ATTENTION. Above R$ 200 thousand, or NOT BUDGETED above R$ 100 thousand: flag EXECUTIVE TEAM and put it at the top.
